verses.zh: 有几个以色列长老到我这里来，坐在我面前。
verses.en: Then some men from Israel’s elders came to me and sat down in front of me.
verses.commentary:
14:1 "elders of Israel" This must refer to tribal leaders already in exile in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 8:1, where
a group of faithful elders were called "elders of Judah"). These particular ones are idolaters (cf. Ezek. 20:1).

This is Judah's problem, her leaders are not faithful YHWHists!

- kings, princes

- priests

- prophets

- elders

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

verses.zh: 耶和华的话就临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，这些人已将他们的假神接到心里，把陷于罪的绊脚石放在面前，我岂能丝毫被他们求问吗？
verses.en: “Son of man, these men have erected their idols in their hearts and placed the obstacle leading to their iniquity[NOTE:1] right before their faces. Should I really allow them to seek[NOTE:2] me?
notes: Heb “the stumbling block of their iniquity.” This phrase is unique to the prophet Ezekiel.
Or “I will not reveal myself to them.” The Hebrew word is used in a technical sense here of seeking an oracle from a prophet (2 Kgs 1:16; 3:11; 8:8).
verses.commentary:
14:3 "these men have set up idols in their hearts" Apparently the idolatry of Jerusalem described in
chapter 8 had already spread to the leaders in exile in Babylon (cf. Ezek. 14:4,6,11; 7:19; 20:7-8). These
elders looked like YHWHists, but in the secret place of their hearts (God knows the heart), they were
corrupted by pagan worship and theology.

The term "idols" comes from several possible roots. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1066, translates
it as "dung balls" (BDB 165, KB 192, NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 864-865) see note at Ezek. 6:4. The
term is used almost exclusively in Ezekiel (39 times) and only once in Jeremiah (i.e. Jer. 50:2) and never in
Isaiah. It originally occurred in the key covenant passages of Lev. 26:30 and Deut. 29:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY

▣ "stumbling block" This term (BDB 506) is used often in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 3:20; 14:3,4,7;
18:30; 21:15; 44:12). Its basic meaning is "to stumble" or "the means by which one stumbles." The origin of
its idiomatic usage comes from

- YHWH's word or covenant was characterized as a clearly marked path (i.e. Ps. 119:105; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- faith originally meant to be stable, walking easily in the path (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

- therefore, to stumble is parallel to leaving the path, to stumbling in the path

This term came to have a Messianic aspect in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 8:14; Rom. 9:33; 1 Pet. 2:8).
The Messiah (the Cornerstone, Gen. 49:24; Ps. 118:22; Isa. 28:16) will become a stumbling block to some.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CORNERSTONE

▣ "Should I be consulted by them at all" This is a grammatically emphatic sentence
(an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB of
the same root [BDB 205, KB 233, Niphal, cf. Ezek. 20:3,31]). The covenant leaders were consulting
idols and false prophets, not YHWH (cf. Ezek. 20:3,21). So why should YHWH now allow them to consult Him?

This VERB has a negative connotation in most of its occurrences in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 14:10; 20:1-4,31).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

verses.zh: 所以你要告诉他们：『主耶和华如此说：以色列家的人中，凡将他的假神接到心里，把陷于罪的绊脚石放在面前，又就了先知来的，我―耶和华在他所求的事上，必按他众多的假神回答他（或译：必按他拜许多假神的罪报应他），
verses.en: Therefore speak to them and say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: When anyone from the house of Israel erects his idols in his heart and sets the obstacle leading to his iniquity before his face, and then consults a prophet, I, the Lord, am determined to answer him personally according to the enormity of his idolatry.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in accordance with the multitude of his idols.”
verses.commentary:
14:4 "speak to them and tell them, ‘Thus says the Lord God'" This is an
emphatic construction.

- a Piel IMPERATIVE, "speak," BDB 180, KB 201

- two Qal PERFECTS, "says," BDB 55, KB 65

YHWH's prophet must address this situation of "apparent" faith!

▣ "I the Lord will be brought to give him an answer" See note at
Ezek. 14:7.

▣ "in the matter" There are three options of how to translate this word (UBS Text Project, p. 38).

- he (idolator) comes (Qere reading BDB 97, KB 112), בא;
Qal PERFECT; same form used earlier
in the verse, NRSV

- "in it" understood as "according to it," בה (MT; UBS Text Project
gives this option a "C" rating)

- "in me," the idolator comes to YHWH, בי (RSV, NEB, NJB, TEV), which results in

- mercy, forgiveness

- judgment (vv. 3,7, Peshitta)

verses.zh: 好在以色列家的心事上捉住他们，因为他们都藉着假神与我生疏。』
verses.en: I will do this in order to capture the hearts of the house of Israel, who have alienated themselves from me on account of all their idols.’
verses.commentary:
14:5 "who are estranged from Me" The VERB "estranged" (BDB 266,
KB 267, Niphal PERFECT) describes the alienation of YHWH's people
from Him because of idolatry. YHWH's people are now strangers/foreigners (cf. Ezek. 7:21; 11:9; 16:22;
28:7,10; 30:12; 31:12) and thus enemies (cf. Isa. 1:4; Ps. 69:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 「所以你要告诉以色列家说：『主耶和华如此说：回头吧！离开你们的偶像，转脸莫从你们一切可憎的事。』
verses.en: “Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Return! Turn from your idols, and turn your faces away from your abominations.
verses.commentary:
14:6 The phrase "Thus says the Lord God" (Adon YHWH) is used in several senses in Ezekiel.

- positive

- a call to repentance, Ezek. 14:6

- forgiveness of the covenant people, Ezek. 36:33

- resurrection, Ezek. 37:12

- gathering exiles, Ezek. 37:21

- restoration of the fortunes of Jacob and having mercy on the whole house of Israel, Ezek. 39:25

- negative

- YHWH gives Ezekiel a message that His people will not listen to, Ezek. 2:4; 3:11

- prophecies against the false prophets, Ezek. 13:3,8

- prophecies against

(1) apostasy, Ezek. 20:30 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: APOSTASY)

(2) social justice, Ezek. 45:9

- prophecies against the surrounding nations

(1) Ammon, Ezek. 25:3

(2) Tyre, Ezek. 28:2

(3) Cush, Put, Lud, Arabia, Libya, Ezek. 30:2-5

(4) Gog, Ezek. 39:1

- prophecies against Judah, Ezek. 5:8; 6:3; 12:19

▣ As Ezek. 14:4 was emphatic, so too, Ezek. 14:6.

- "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "say" ‒ BDB 55, KB 65, Qal PERFECT

YHWH commands them to do three things (all using one VERBAL root,
BDB 996, KB 1427).

- repent" (cf. Ezek. 18:30,32; 33:11; Isa. 55:6-7)

- "turn away from your idols"

- "turn away from all your abominations"

SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

verses.zh: 因为以色列家的人，或在以色列中寄居的外人，凡与我隔绝，将他的假神接到心里，把陷于罪的绊脚石放在面前，又就了先知来要为自己的事求问我的，我―耶和华必亲自回答他。
verses.en: For when anyone from the house of Israel, or the resident foreigner[NOTE:1] who lives in Israel, separates himself from me and erects his idols in his heart and sets the obstacle leading to his iniquity before his face, and then consults a prophet to seek something from me, I, the Lord, am determined to answer him personally.
notes: The ger (גֵּר) “resident foreigner” had a different status in different countries. In Israel the foreigners going by this term are (or are supposed to be) fully integrated into Israel’s social fabric and worshipers of Yahweh. Such an attachment to the Lord is a prior condition to the possibility of separating from the Lord. See also the notes at Exod 12:19 and Deut 29:11.
verses.commentary:
14:7 "the immigrants" Non-Jews were to be treated as equals in the legal realm (cf. Lev. 19:33-34,35).
Israel was to deal with them graciously (cf. Lev. 23:22; Deut. 10:19; 24:17; 27:19). Israel had also been an
alien in Egypt (cf. Exod. 22:21; 23:9) and knew how it felt (cf. Deut. 16:11)! But, they were required to function within Israel's faith
(i.e. Exod. 12:19; Lev. 16:29; 17:8; Num. 9:14; Deut. 1:16; 16:11)

However, in this context, these immigrants are viewed in a negative sense as someone who claimed to
worship YHWH but retained their pagan origins in their hearts. These foreigners were

- from the Exodus of Egypt (i.e. "mixed multitudes," cf. Exod. 12:38; Num. 11:4)

- those who migrated to Canaan

- neighbors in the exilic community in Babylon who brought idolatry into the covenant community

▣ "who separates himself from Me" This VERB (BDB 634,
KB 684, Niphal IMPERFECT) means to dedicate oneself by separating
oneself from ceremonial evil. The NOUN form is used of those in Numbers 6 who
separate themselves by vow and restrictions to YHWH (i.e. Nazirites, both male and female). There is a
play on words here.

- "holy," means separated to God for His service

- those who separate themselves (men and women) to God by special vow (Numbers 6).

- these idolaters have separated themselves from God to idols

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAZIRITE VOW

▣ "I the Lord will be brought to answer him in My own person" What an
ominous phrase. YHWH comes personally, not for blessing, but for destruction (cf. Ezek. 14:4; also note
Heb. 10:31).

verses.zh: 我必向那人变脸，使他作了警戒，笑谈，令人惊骇，并且我要将他从我民中剪除；你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: I will set my face against that person and will make him an object lesson and a byword[NOTE:1] and will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
verses.commentary:
14:8 "I shall set My face against that man" As the idolater sets his idol "right before his face"
(cf. Ezek. 14:4), so now YHWH sets His face against him (cf. Ezek. 15:7). The face (BDB 815) is an idiom
of personal presence (cf. Ezek. 14:4,7).

Notice what YHWH threatens to do to the idolater.

- make him a sign (BDB 16)

- make him a proverb (BDB 605, possibly "byword," cf. Deut. 28:37; 1 Kgs. 9:7; 2 Chr. 7:20; Ps. 44:14;
Jer. 24:9; Joel 2:17)

- cut him off from the covenant people (BDB 503, KB 500, Hiphil PERFECT)

verses.zh: 先知若被迷惑说一句预言，是我―耶和华任那先知受迷惑，我也必向他伸手，将他从我民以色列中除灭。
verses.en: “‘As for the prophet, if he is made a fool by being deceived into speaking a prophetic word—I, the Lord, have made a fool of[NOTE:1] that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
notes: The translation is uncertain due to difficulty both in determining the meaning of the verb’s stem and its conjugation in this context. In the Qal stem the basic meaning of the verbal root פָּתַה (patah) is “to be gullible, foolish.” The doubling stems (the Pual and Piel used in this verse) typically give such stative verbs a factitive sense, hence either “make gullible” (i.e., “entice”) or “make into a fool” (i.e., “to show to be a fool”). The latter represents the probable meaning of the term in Jer 20:7, 10 and is followed here (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:193; R. Mosis “Ez 14, 1-11 - ein Ruf zur Umkehr,” BZ 19 [1975]: 166-69; and ThWAT 4:829-31). In this view, if a prophet speaks when not prompted by God, he will be shown to be a fool, but this does not reflect negatively on the Lord because it is God who shows him to be a fool. Secondly, the verb is in the perfect conjugation and may be translated as “I have made a fool of him” or “I have enticed him,” or to show determination (see IBHS 439-41 §27.2f and g), or in certain syntactical constructions as future. Any of these may be plausible if the doubling stems used are understood in the sense of “making a fool of.” But if understood as “to make gullible,” more factors come into play. As the Hebrew verbal form is a perfect, it is often translated as present perfect: “I have enticed.” In this case the Lord states that he himself enticed the prophet to cooperate with the idolaters. Such enticement to sin would seem to be a violation of God’s moral character, but sometimes he does use such deception and enticement to sin as a form of punishment against those who have blatantly violated his moral will (see, e.g., 2 Sam 24). If one follows this line of interpretation in Ezek 14:9, one would have to assume that the prophet had already turned from God in his heart. However, the context gives no indication of this. Therefore, it is better to take the perfect as indicating certitude and to translate it with the future tense: “I will entice.” In this case the Lord announces that he will judge the prophet appropriately. If a prophet allows himself to be influenced by idolaters, then the Lord will use deception as a form of punishment against that deceived prophet. A comparison with the preceding oracles also favors this view. In 14:4 the perfect of certitude is used for emphasis (see “I will answer”), though in v. 7 a participle is employed. For a fuller discussion of this text, see R. B. Chisholm, Jr., “Does God Deceive?” BSac 155 (1998): 23-25.
verses.commentary:
14:9 YHWH reveals Himself to true prophets, but hides His word from false prophets. He uses even them for His
own purposes (i.e. 1 Kgs. 22:22-23). These false prophets were prophesying "peace" and "security" (cf. Jer. 14:15), but they
were lying! The refusal of Judah to repent caused YHWH's judgment to come!

YHWH uses even "evil" for His purposes and plans! One way the ancient Hebrew Scriptures
demonstrated monotheism was by attributing all causality to God (i.e. Deut. 32:39; Job 5:18; 12:13-25;
Isa. 30:26; 45:7; Hosea 6:1; Amos 3:6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

▣ "My hand" See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

verses.zh: 他们必担当自己的罪孽。先知的罪孽和求问之人的罪孽都是一样，
verses.en: They will bear their punishment;[NOTE:1] the punishment of the one who sought an oracle will be the same as the punishment of the prophet who gave it[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “They will bear responsibility for their iniquity.” The Hebrew term “iniquity” (three times in this verse) often refers by metonymy to the consequence of sin (see Gen 4:13).
Or “As is the guilt of the inquirer, so is the guilt of the prophet.”

verses.zh: 好使以色列家不再走迷离开我，不再因各样的罪过玷污自己，只要作我的子民，我作他们的　神。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: so that the house of Israel will no longer go astray from me, nor continue to defile themselves by all their sins. They will be my people, and I will be their God,[NOTE:1] declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
notes: I will be their God. See Exod 6:7; Lev 26:12; Jer 7:23; 11:4.
verses.commentary:
14:11 The purpose of judgment is restoration (cf. Ezek. 14:22-23)! However, for this to occur, some
other things must happen first.

- "Israel may no longer stray" (BDB 1073, KB 1766, Qal IMPERFECT,
cf. Ezek. 44:10,15; 48:11)

- Israel "no longer defile themselves" (BDB 379, KB 375, Hithpael
IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 37:23)

If these criteria are not met, then they will not be His covenant people (cf. Ezek. 11:20; 34:30;
36:28; 37:27; Exod. 6:7; Lev. 11:45; 22:33; 25:38; 26:12,44,45). The covenant promises are conditional on
covenant obedience (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28; 30:1,15,19).

Passages such as this cause me to question if the modern state of Israel is truly the Israel
of Promise. They are a secular, European-type, state government. Very few Jews keep or practice the Mosaic
Law. The promises to Israel were conditional!

For a good YouTube video on this subject, see Steve Gregg, The Modern State of Israel

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

▣ "they will be My people, and I shall be their God" This is covenant language (cf. Lev. 26:12;
Jer. 7:23; 11:4; 30:22; 31:33; 32:38; Ezek. 11:20; 14:11; 36:28; 37:23,27).

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，若有一国犯罪干犯我，我也向他伸手折断他们的杖，就是断绝他们的粮，使饥荒临到那地，将人与牲畜从其中剪除；
verses.en: “Son of man, suppose a country sins against me by being unfaithful and I stretch out my hand against it, cut off its bread supply,[NOTE:1] cause famine to come on it, and kill both people and animals.
verses.commentary:
14:13 The Jewish Study Bible marginal note (p. 1066) asserts that the "ifs" of Ezek. 14:13,15,17,19 are
textual markers for a legal case (i.e. casuistic law).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

▣ "committing unfaithfulness" This VERB (BDB 591,
KB 612, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) comes from the priestly realm and
denotes

- acts of idolatrous treachery (i.e. idolatry)

- marital infidelity in Num. 5:12,27

- in Ezekiel for unfaithfulness towards YHWH (cf. Ezek. 15:8; 17:20; 18:24; 20:27; 39:23,26)

This phrase is emphatic by the repetition of the Hebrew root (BDB 591) in the
INFINITIVE and the NOUN.

Notice YHWH's reactions.

- "I stretch out My hand against it" (i.e. His nation, His capital), which is an idiom of purposeful action

- "I destroy (lit. "break the staff," cf. Ezek. 4:16; 5:16) its supply of bread," which denotes famine

- "I send famine against it"

- "I cut off (i.e. destroy completely) from it both man and beast" (cf. Ezek. 14:7,19,21)

- "cause wild beasts to pass through the land" (Ezek. 14:15, cf. Lev. 26:22)

- "bring a sword on that country"

- "send a plague against that country" (Ezek. 14:19)

All of them are summarized in four severe judgments (Ezek. 14:21; 5:12; Deut. 32:23-24)

- sword (BDB 352)

- famine (BDB 944)

- wild beasts (BDB 312, cf. Lev. 26:22)

- plague (BDB 184)

Many of these reflect the covenant warnings of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28.

verses.zh: 其中虽有挪亚、但以理、约伯这三人，他们只能因他们的义救自己的性命。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel,[NOTE:1] and Job, were in it, they would save only their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Sovereign Lord.
notes: Traditionally this has been understood as a reference to the biblical Daniel, though he was still quite young when Ezekiel prophesied. One wonders if he had developed a reputation as an intercessor by this point. For this reason some prefer to see a reference to a ruler named Danel, known in Canaanite legend for his justice and wisdom. In this case all three of the individuals named would be non-Israelites, however the Ugaritic Danel is not known to have qualities of faith in the Lord that would place him in the company of the other men. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:447-50.
verses.commentary:
14:14 "even though these three men" It is clear from the OT who Noah (cf. Genesis 6-9) and
Job (cf. Job) are. It is not so clear who Daniel (BDB 193) is.

- the father-in-law of Enoch, Jubilees 4:20, who surprisingly is not mentioned as an ancient
righteous person

- a son of David, 1 Chr. 3:1

- a priest of the line of Ithamar, Ezra 8:2; Neh. 10:7

- a well known Canaanite sage, Ezek. 14:14,20; 28:3

- a prophet, hero, administrator under Nebuchadnezzar II from the biblical book of Daniel

- an unknown famous righteous person

The biblical Daniel is a contemporary with Ezekiel and may not have had time for his faith and life to be well
known (i.e. become a proverb of wisdom and faithfulness). Daniel might really be Danel (or Dan-El, Ezekiel's
spelling is different from Dan. 6:16 and is spelled like the hero of the Ugaritic text), a Canaanite sage (from Ras Shamra
Ugaritic texts) known for his upright thoughtful life. If this identification is true, then all three examples were not directly related to Abraham.

The problem is that he is involved with the Canaanite pantheon! Therefore, even with all the questions the biblical Daniel seems
the best option (cf. Ezek. 28:3). For more historical information of the identity of "Danil," see IVP Biblical Background Commentary (OT), p. 700.

▣ "by their own righteousness they could only deliver themselves" This phrase reflects
OT theology of a performance-based righteousness (cf. Ezek. 3:21, or better an OT sense of "blamelessness,
like Noah," Gen. 6:9 or Job, Job 1:1). This section is a theological precursor to chapter 18. The people
thought that a few faithful worshipers of YHWH would cause YHWH to withhold His wrath (like Gen. 18:22-33,
also note Jer. 15:1-4), but this proved not to be true!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLAMELESS, INNOCENT, GUILTLESS, WITHOUT REPROACH

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

The term "deliver" (BDB 664, KB 717, Piel IMPERFECT) in
the Piel, usually means "to strip off" in the sense of "plunder" (cf. Exod. 3:22; 12:36; 2 Chr. 20:25).
Only here is it translated "deliver" or "save," although the Niphal (cf. Ezek. 14:16,18)
and Hiphil (cf. Ezek. 3:19,21; 14:20; 33:19; 34:10) stems have this sense.

A righteous person (in the OT Mosaic sense, cf. Ezek. 3:20-21; 14:12-20; 18:5-32; 33:12-20)
can only deliver himself/herself. OT righteousness is not transferable to others. It is an individual
performance-based covenant.

verses.zh: 我若使恶兽经过糟践那地，使地荒凉，以致因这些兽，人都不得经过；
verses.en: “Suppose I were to send wild animals through the land and kill its children, leaving it desolate, without travelers due to the wild animals.
verses.commentary:
14:15

NASB, JPSOA
"depopulate"

NKJV
"empty"

NRSV
"ravage"

TEV
"kill"

NJB
"rob it of its children"

REB
"destroy the population"

Peshitta
"destroy it"

LXX
"take vengeance"

The NJB captures the essence of the VERB (BDB 1013,
KB 1491, Piel PERFECT). This is part of the covenant curses (cf., Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 28). If the Israelites violate YHWH's covenant, their children will die (no posterity, no family joy).

- by sword, Deut. 32:35; 1 Sam. 15:33; Lam. 1:20

- by wild beasts, Lev. 26:22; Ezek. 5:17; 14:15

verses.zh: 虽有这三人在其中，主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，他们连儿带女都不能得救，只能自己得救，那地仍然荒凉。
verses.en: Even if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, they could not save their own sons or daughters; they would save only their own lives, and the land would become desolate.

verses.zh: 或者我使刀剑临到那地，说：刀剑哪，要经过那地，以致我将人与牲畜从其中剪除；
verses.en: “Or suppose I were to bring a sword against that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and I were to kill both people and animals.
verses.commentary:
14:17 "Let the sword pass through" This VERB (BDB 716, KB 778) is
a Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense.
The sword (i.e. invasion and exile) became the will and command of YHWH against His own covenant people!

verses.zh: 虽有这三人在其中，主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，他们连儿带女都不能得救，只能自己得救。
verses.en: Even if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, they could not save their own sons or daughters—they would save only their own lives.

verses.zh: 或者我叫瘟疫流行那地，使我灭命（原文是带血）的忿怒倾在其上，好将人与牲畜从其中剪除；
verses.en: “Or suppose I were to send a plague into that land and pour out my rage on it with bloodshed, killing both people and animals.

verses.zh: 虽有挪亚、但以理、约伯在其中，主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，他们连儿带女都不能救，只能因他们的义救自己的性命。」
verses.en: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, they could not save their own son or daughter; they would save only their own lives by their righteousness.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「我将这四样大灾―就是刀剑、饥荒、恶兽、瘟疫降在耶路撒冷，将人与牲畜从其中剪除，岂不更重吗？
verses.en: “For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: How much worse will it be when I send my four terrible judgments—sword, famine, wild animals, and plague—to Jerusalem[NOTE:1] to kill both people and animals!
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
14:21 The four judgments mentioned were common in the ancient world (i.e. Lev. 26:22,25-26; they are also
mentioned in the Babylonian flood texts).

verses.zh: 然而其中必有剩下的人，他们连儿带女必带到你们这里来，你们看见他们所行所为的，要因我降给耶路撒冷的一切灾祸，便得了安慰。
verses.en: Yet some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out. They will come out to you, and when you see their behavior and their deeds, you will be consoled about the catastrophe I have brought on Jerusalem—for everything I brought on it.
verses.commentary:
14:22-23 The terrible judgments on Judah and Jerusalem were for the purpose of redemption! A new Israel
will rise out of the ashes of the old rebellious one. There will be a believing remnant (cf. Ezek. 6:7-9; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT [three senses]).
There will be days of repentance (cf. Ezek. 14:6; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT])!
There will be a new day of righteousness (cf. Isaiah 55-66).

The tragedy is that even restored Judah/Israel (Ezra, Nehemiah) could not keep the Mosaic Law.
The Law's function is clearly spelled out in Galatians 3. The performance-based covenant must become the grace-based
"new covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34, described in Ezek. 36:22-36. Fallen humanity cannot approach a holy God with
personal righteousness (cf. Eph. 2:8-9)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSAIC LAW AND THE CHRISTIAN

14:22 "you will see their conduct and actions" This phrase has been interpreted two contrasting ways.

- the wicked receive their just judgment ("actions," BDB 760 is always used in a negative sense)

- the wicked are changed by YHWH's judgment and repent (cf. Ezek. 18:21-23)

The question is, does this refer to an illustration of God's justice or an example of a believing,
faithful remnant?

It is possible that the message to the exiles was "the current generation does not have to
bear the sins of their fathers" (or fellow Israelites). Each person's personal faith and action (cf. Ezekiel 18)
will determine one's relationship with YHWH. This is a rare example of an individual emphasis in a corporate
society. This will form a crucial aspect of "new" covenant theology (cf. John 1:12; 3:16; Rom. 10:9-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: What Does It Mean to "Receive," "Believe," "Confess/Profess," and "Call Upon?"

verses.en: They will console you when you see their behavior and their deeds, because you will know that it was not without reason that I have done everything that I have done in it, declares the Sovereign Lord.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 14:1-5

1Then some elders of Israel came to me and sat down before me. 2And the word of
the Lord came to me, saying, 3"Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts and have put right before their
faces the stumbling block of their iniquity. Should I be consulted by them at all? 4Therefore speak to them and tell them, 'Thus says the Lord
